newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle surge to higher end, new contract highs.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle surge to higher end, new contract highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures surged to sharply higher closes as heavy fund buying sent all months to contract highs while feeder cattle futures finished just below an earlier 40-month high for the nearby month, dealers said.
All feeder cattle contracts also set new contract highs.

Dealers said Cargill Investor Services and Merrill Lynch were featured buyers of August live cattle and LFG, FIMAT Futures, R.B.& H. Financial Services, E.D. and F. Man International and LIT were all buyers of October.
Gains were boosted by news that higher prices had been paid in the cash market, with active trade at Plains area feedlots reported at $64.00 per cwt, up $2.00 from last week.
USDA also reported that one pen traded in north Texas at $65.00 per cwt and there was market talk that a pen also traded in Oklahoma at $65.00.
Dealers said Lind Waldock and ADM Investor Services were noted sellers of August live cattle and Refco a featured seller of October.
August live cattle closed 0.800 cent a lb higher at 66.650 cents, just below an earlier contract high of 66.900 cents. Other months were up 0.850 to 0.450 cents.
Feeder cattle were also higher, aided by spillover strength from the live cattle pit and lower corn prices.
August feeders rose to a contract high of 82.300 cents per lb, the highest level for the nearby contract since March 1994. August closed up 1.275 cent at 82.100 cents.
Dealers said Rosenthal Collins was a noted buyer of August with Smith Barney featured on the sell side. Other months, which also set contract highs, ended up 1.250 to 0.900 cent.
In live cattle options there was commission house short covering of August calls with strike prices from 65 to 68 cents and commercial buying of August 64 cent puts.
Beef trimmings futures were higher with Lind Waldock a featured buyer. August closed up 1.20 cent a lb at 49.50 cents.
Dealers noted interest in buying August trimmings/selling August live cattle.
Boneless beef futures were also higher with ADM Investor Services a buyer in October, which finished up 1.50 cent at 97.00 cents.
